properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/26/2024 to SWN PROD CO LLC in Herrick Township, Bradford county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SWN PROD CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/26/2024
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8180971
Permit API: 015-23842
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Herrick Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/26/2024
Comments: Southwestern's (SWN's) reported to the DEP reporting hotline at ~ 1705 hours on 03/22/2024 that a vendor ripped containment liner while moving hoses during demobilization activities. Ponded rain water ran from containment onto newly exposed soil/gravel. It is believed rainwater came into contact with brine contaminated site equipment releasing approx. 20 to 30 gallons.On 03/26/2024 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection of SWN's VanOrder-Patrick (12 Pad) Well Pad located in Herrick Township, Bradford County. The weather was 47 degrees and partly cloudy. I arrived at 1010 hours. This inspection was conducted in response to a release reported to DEP by SWN.On 03/26/2024 I spoke with Mike Deming a SWN representative who said the release was ~1-2 barrels. Photos #2-6 show the progression of the remediation process from 03/22/2024 to 03/26/2024. SWN reported that the highest conductivity reading after the release was ~21 mS/cm. The red dumpster seen in photo #6 is lined and holds the recovered material. Due to active operations during the time of this inspection access to the spill area was not possible. SWN representatives were present during the time of the inspection. SWN representatives said they are currently working on drill outs. They have completed the plugs for one of the three new wells. They plan to finish within two weeks. Pooled water on the pad was field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) between 428-839 us/cm. Pooled water within the off loading secondary containment was field measured for EC at ~ 2.7 mS/cm. The DEP reported the findings to SWN representatives who said that it would be taken care of right away. Based on the reported release quantity this is being referred to Act 2 for compliance. Based on the reported release violations of the following are cited against API #015-23842 at this time:35 P.S. 691.402(b)35 P.S. 6018.30125 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)I departed at 1050 hours.

Comments: On 02/03/2023, a routine complete inspection of the Cox 1 well site was conducted.During the inspection the following was observed:-Well tags were observed on the wellhead (Photo 1).-The well and operator's information was displayed and visible at the well site as required by OGA 3211(g) (Photo 2).-Some corrosion was observed on the well production equipment (Photos 1-3).-Elevated conductivity was observed within the substrate underneath pipes associated with the production tank (Photos 4-6). The tank is within the earthen secondary containment. -A battery without secondary containment was observed. The Department recommends the battery be placed on secondary containment (Photo 7).-What appeared to possibly be grease, associated with the pump jack, was observed on the substrate near the wellhead (Photo 8, within red rectangle). The Department recommends the removal and proper disposal of the affected substrate and ensuring the pump jack is monitored to avoid potential contamination of the ground. No violation.Determination: Regarding the observed elevated conductivity associated with the production tank piping, violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.57(a), and 91.34(a) are being issued for the release of production fluid to the ground.

Unconventional: Yes

Comments: On 12/06/2024, an incident inspection was conducted at the Henderson Well Site following receipt of an incident report, submitted on 12/04/2024, following a spill (CTS 385605). I was accompanied by DJ Hardy (EQT).On 12/04/2024, it was reported that approximately 20 gallons of brine water was spilled on the well pad following a dump line washout. EQT intends to remediate through Act 2 guidelines. EQT shared that it did not appear that there were any impacts off of the pad and the sumps did not appear impacted. The following was observed:The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance and the emergency response plan was in the mailbox (Photo 1).Material had been excavated from around the dump line behind the 15H Gas Production Unit (GPU) (Photos 2, 3). The elbow joint on the dump line was the origin of the spill (Photos 4, 5).Conductivity readings around the origin were 2.25, 2.37, and 6.26 mS/cm (Photos 6-8).The main dump line was also exposed with material excavated (Photo 9).Readings along the main dump line were 2.28, 4.04, 4.57, 5.56, and 7.28 mS/cm (Photos 10-14).A test pit was excavated to determine the extent of impacted material. The pit was filled and no elevated conductivity was noted in the area (Photo 15).No stressed vegetation noted and no elevated conductivity within vegetation (Photo 16). Bank was cut for access.A vac truck removed material from the excavated pits and was in a container on site (Photo 17).Additional material labeled was on site (Photos 18, 19).Due to the release of production fluid to to pad, violations of 78a.54, SWMA 301, 78a.57(a), and 91.34(a) are being issued.

Inspection Date: 2020-05-27
Comments: On 5/27/2020 at approximately 1030, a follow-up inspection was conducted in response to violations issued on 4/12/2019 (Inspection 2882118). I was accompanied by PA DEP James Kulha. Per the 12/10/2019 letter, the Department has approved the Final Report/remedial Action Completion Report" submitted for the Alternative Remediation of this site. Conductivity was measured in various locations around the well and brine tank and do not appear to be significantly elevated. Vegetation growth adjacent to the brine tank remains distressed (Photo# 9). The Department recommends adding additional seed/mulch to the area. A discarded oil drum was observed on the site next to a brine tank that does not appear to be in use. The drum is labeled "Conklin oil + sand" and appears to be leaking. A petroleum odor was observed in the area (Photos#3-6). The Department recommends that this waste drum and affected soil be removed to prevent further contamination. A slope failure was observed adjacent to the well site (Photo# 7). The Department recommends that this slope failure be temporarily stabilized and remediated in order to achieve site stabilization. A leak was observed on the concrete below the pump jack (Photo# 10). The Department recommends that the well equipment be inspected and the leaked substance be cleaned up to prevent further contamination at the site. Violations are recurring at the site with regards to fluid disposal. Additionally, violations are being issued in regards to the observed slope failure.

Comments: Inspection 1 of 2:On 01/24/2025, an incident inspection was conducted a the EQT R. Smith Well site in Carroll Township, Washington County in response to a spill reported by the operator on 01/23/2025.The operator reported that the check valve cracked resulting in a spill. Approximately 5 gallons of produced water.EQT, Moody and SPSI was on site during spill remediation. EQT stated to the department onsite that this spill will be going ACT 2 due to additional observations.The following was observed during inspection:- The Act 9 sign was located at the access road entrance in accordance with 78a55 requirements. Emergency Response Plan (ERP) was on site in mailbox (Photo 1)-Well site entrance and access road appear to be maintained (Photo 2).-I observed fluid actively flowing within well pad drainage. EQT stated to the department that the valves were shut off once spill was found (Photo 4 and 5).-Roll off dumpster was observed onsite for spill remediation. Additional roll of dumpster was delivered during inspection (Photo 7,8,19).-13H GPU check valve resulted in the spill. SPSI was actively remediating and removing impacted material during inspection. Spill occurred between 5H and 13H GPU. Impacted material and elevated readings were found along 5H and 13H GPU. I observed GPU wasn't within secondary containment (Photo 9-15).-Equipment access road was underneath and along 21H GPU and additional GPUs (Photo 16-18).-Well head and well sign was observed (Photo 20).-It appears the spill reached the well pad drainage outlets. I observed elevated conductivity readings of 3.07 mS/cm, 5.17 mS/cm, 5.82 mS/cm and 6.14 mS/cm - 200 ft from GPU spill location at the drainage outlet and collection channel. It appears Waters of the Commonwealth is impacted (Photo 21-25).Field scout conductivity probe was calibrated on 01/24/25 before inspection was conducted.Violations are being issued for: 78a57(a), SWMA 301, 78a.54, 91.34(a), CSL 301, CSL 307(a).

Comments: This inspection report has been developed to document an on-site routine complete inspect, and to summarize the overall status of this well and well location. The project was recently acquired by Big Dog Energy, LLC. Applications for the transfer of all three wells permitted on the site, from Geopetro LLC to Big Dog Energy LLC, were received by the Department on August 2, 2021. An application for the transfer of the ESCGP that is currently active on the site was also received by the Department. The current Operator information has not yet been updated in the Department's electronic database. Well number 019-21927, along with two other wells, (API ID#'s: 019-21948, 019-21947), were drilled and currently exist on the location. Although the Act Nine sign has been changed to reflect the current owner of the well location, the well tags have not yet been updated. Updated well tags should be installed on each of the wells at some point in the near future. Inspection ID number's 2092885, 2092888, and 2092893 (conducted on August 17, 2012) suggests that all of the wells have been stimulated. Subsequent inspections have indicated that the wells have been on inactive status since at least December of 2013. ESCGP number ESX11-019-0109 is currently active on the site. The permit was renewed by RE Gas in 2017 and is set to expire on 08/07/2022. None of the earthwork proposed in the plan was ever implemented in the field. Up until very recently, the property owner had been grazing cattle on the site and using the tank pad as a feedlot. A small sediment slide had developed on the cut bank surface to the east of the well location. With the exception of the slide, there are currently no clear E&S or stabilization-related issues associated with the site. Big Dog is currently preparing all of the wells on this site to be placed into production. A contractor hired by Big Dog was working on establishing new barbed wire fencing around the location when this inspection was conducted. Some production equipment, including 3 GPU's are being staged on the site. The slip on the cut surface above the location was discussed with the contractor. Containment under the GPU's was also discussed, as well as updated well tags.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/24/2022
Comments: Site inspection by EPS Justin Abbott. Inspection conducted in response to spill notification submitted by EQT for the COP Tract 551-B pad. Inspection accompanied by EQT Lead EHS Coordinator Mark Barbier. Meeting on site with EQT Company Man Mike Hood. Weather conditions at time of inspection are partly cloudy, humid and 73 degrees F. Well stimulation activity is ceased at this time while EQT reviews SOPs.According to the Standard Detail Report, the spill notification was submitted by Mr. Barbier. At around 0800 hours, US Well Services was swabbing the well to switch over from the 6H to the 7H well. At that time, the open topped blender hopper overflowed releasing an estimated 140 barrels of fluid to containment, of which an unknown quantity of fluid overtopped the containment structures. During discussions on site with Mr. Barbier, the estimation was based on the fact that the pumps may have been releasing 20 barrels per minute for 7 minutes, although the exact volume can not be determined. The Department conducted conductivity screenings using an Oakton PCTS 50 meter and a Hanna Groline Soil Conductivity meter. Pooled fluid remaining within the containment structure was observed with conductivity readings between 7-8 mS/cm. Fluid within the north pad ditch and sumps outside of containment ranged from 3.92-5.37 mS/cm. Visual evidence of spilled fluid extended from a brushy area at the north conrer of the pad, along the entire ditch perimeter into the woods at the eastern corner of the pad where appeared to collect in a row of silt sock. Two vac trucks are present on site. One truck is vacuuming fluid from containment, a second truck is pumping spilled fluid collecting at he low point in the eastern corner of the pad ditch (photo 9). Visual observations near the blender unit indicated that fluid was released with sufficient force to release frac sand from the hopper. Two drums of frac sand were hand shoveled from the spill area (photo 10). Friction reducer material was also observed on pad rock outside containment. On the pad surface, spilled fluid is observed leaking through pad rock under the working tank secondary containment (photo 5). Pad rock affected by spilled fluid under containment is estimated to cover an area of 250 feet in length by 25-40 feet in width. Violation ID: 886008
Permit API: 083-55763
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-06-03
Comments: This well is a producing combination well with an electric powered motor attached. The well was being operated at the time of this inspection. The stuffing box gasket failed, and at the time of visit, the well was pumping oil and brine out to the ground. The fluid plus runoff from recent rains allowed the oil to flow down the road approximately 150 feet, entering a puddle near a culvert that carried an UNT Chappel Fork. The operator was contacted to get cleanup efforts underway. The well was shut off and pads were placed down to collect as much oil from the track as possible. No oil was apparent in the UNT. Rain stopped and there was a decrease in the flow of oil down the track. The pumper for this lease showed up and was able to leave and get a vacuum truck to come collect the water/oil in the puddle. Marking tape was placed so that public vehicles would not drive through the oil. It is estimated that 15-20 gallons of fluid, including 3-5 gallons of oil were released from the well due to the stuffing box failure. Most pooled in a low spot next to the wellhead. Some ran down the access road, again pooling in a puddle of water that was previously mentioned. The brine mostly stayed in place in the soil or vegetation. A puddle within 10 feet of the wellhead showed over 20 mS/cm conductivity, while checking further toward the extent of the spill showed much lower numbers. The final puddle registered under 0.1 mS/cm. The operator had the vac truck on the way and after later discussions, it was decided that they would need to excavate the area around the wellhead to remove impacted soil. Further follow up will be done on this site as possible.

Comments: On March 25, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of the Cowden 6H gas well located on the Cowden 16 well pad in Hopewell Twp, Washington Co. Due to database error, this inspection report lists the Farm Name and Well # as the Cowden 9H OG Well. Present during today's inspection is DEP WQS Tyler Metzger and Big Dog Energy representative Mr. Scott.Mr.Anderson/BDE is reportedly the agent intending to operate the gas wells on the Cowden 16 well pad, however, according to DEP records, Diversified owns both the gas wells on the pad and the well pad.This inspection is following IR 4139756, where violations were issued for failure to have ERP on site and for failure to remove production equipment not in use/connected to other equipment or a gas well.At the time of this inspection, Mr. Scott notified the Department that a crane was on site to remove the white structure from the Cowden 16 well pad.At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed an Act 9 sign at the access road entrance, the DEP notes that despite being unaware of a pending transfer of ownership, all information that is required to be posted on the Act 9 sign appears to be BDE's. Both on-site mailboxes which were attached to the Act 9 sign were observed to be empty at the time of this inspection. During IR 4139756, Mr. Anderson stated that an updated Emergency Response Plan is expected to be on site within the next 10 days. Violations issued to the 6H gas well for failure to have the ERP on site are being continued at this time.At the time of this inspection, it does not appear that any of the wells at the Cowden well site are in production yet (the 6H, 10H, and 16H). At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a white above ground storage tank on the graveled well pad, the Department did not observe this tank to be connected to gas wells or any other production equipment on the Cowden 16 well pad. At the time of this inspection, the Department also observed additional production equipment that did not appear to be connected to anyother production equipment or any wells on the well pad. At the time of this inspection, a white structure that during IR 4139756 was not observed to be connected to any other production equipment or wells on site was observed to be actively being removed from the gravel well pad. In IR 4139756, the Department requested a written timeline for when all equipment, tanks, and structures not necessary for the production of the well(s) on the Cowden 16 well pad will be removed and when any equipment, tanks and structures necessary for production will be connected. The Department requested this written timeline be provided to the Department by COB 3/13/2026. No response has been received to date.Violations issued to the 6H gas well for failure to remove equipment, tanks, and structures not necessary for the production of the well(s) on the Cowden 16 well pad are being continued at this time as the white structure was the only equipment observed to be removed from the site at this time.At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed a well tag fixed to the 6H gas well with all required information posted on it. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of the 6H gas well at this time.Based on today's inspection, violations issued to the 6H gas well for failure to have ERP on site and for failure to remove production equipment not in use/connected to other equipment or a gas well are being continued at this time.

Comments: This well was drilled in a forested area off of South Enterline Road in July 1997. Violations were issued during the previous inspection due to a spill from a hole in the bottom of the brine tank. Since that initial inspection, work has been started associated with the cleanup of the site. The brine tank has been removed, and contaminated soil has been excavated from the area of the spill. This contaminated soil has been placed on plastic and protected from the weather and remains on site near the wellhead. Conductivity readings taken during this inspection indicate that a small area of contaminated soil remains to be removed upslope from the current excavation area. When the remaining contaminated soil has been removed, fresh topsoil should be used to fill in this area, and mulch should be used to stabilize the area for the winter. Comments: On August 13, 2025 the Department conducted a Follow Up inspection of the Diamond 3 plugged well site located in Nicholson Township, Fayette County following IR 3982260 where violations were continued for failure to restore a plugged well site within 9 months of plugging as well as in response to a third-party notification Department received from Diversified representative Heather Empfield (documented in IR 4036386). This well was reportedly plugged on 3/13/2024, therefore the well site shall be fully restored by 12/13/2024 in accordance with current regulations. A stabilized access road comprised of dirt and gravel was observed and is noted to remain as it services a compressor station located beyond the Diamond 3 plugged site.Upon inspection of the Diamond 3 plugged well site, the Department observed the beginning portion of the plugged well site which is located right off of the access road, to be comprised of dead vegetation. The location and nature of this dead vegetation supports Diversified's claims of third party disturbance consisting of the spraying of weed killer and mowing of remaining vegetation in this location. The Department observed the remaining portion of the plugged well site that is away from the access road to be exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. A silt fence was also observed to still be installed along the back edge of the plugged well site. No erosion or sedimentation issues were observed at this plugged well site at this time.Based on today's inspection, violations issued for failure to restore the plugged well site shall remain outstanding at this time pending the removal of all erosion and sediment control features. Transmittal of this inspection report is delayed due to an inspection app IT error.

Comments: On May 27 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in regards to violations issued under inspection report 4065561. This gas well is currently under an Order (Enf ID 442909). This inspection is not evaluating the operator's compliance with the Order.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the Department again observed piping which ran to/from the production tank and the valve near the bottom of the tank, both of which appeared to be heavily corroded. While these readings appear lower than readings obtained in IR 4065561 and IR 4095943, they still appear slightly elevated in comparison to the background reading of 0.23mS.The operator previously provided a response regarding the release on 10/2/2025 stating the following:"Our plan to correct this is as follows: Have brine hauled away, repair lines leading to tank, cause is just age, paint well, Schedule for completion of these repairs will depend on availably of hauling company. Well painting will need to be completed in accordance with weather conditions once other repairs are completed. we expect repairs should be completed within 90 days".It did not appear any remediation efforts have been conducted at the time of the inspection.Based on today's inspection, violations are outstanding.

Comments: On 10/11/2024, I conducted an inspection at the Blacksville I BIP32 Well in Wayne Township, Greene County in response to a Notice of Intent (NOI) to plug a well The NOI was received by The Department on 9/9/2024 and 10/1/2024 due to plugging schedule changes.On site at the time of inspection were contractors associated with well plugging. The contractors indicated that the plugging rig was set up on 10/8/2024, and they expected the plugging operation to take 3 days to complete.While on site I observed the following:-The access road appeared to be in generally good condition. I recommend that the Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) installed along the access road receive additional aggregate if contractors expect to be on site for additional time (Photos 1-6).-I observed a silt fence filled with sediment at STA 14+00. I observed sediment that bypassed the silt fence at STA 14+00 and entered a stream identified by E and S plans as UNT to Dunkard Creek. Scouring left of the culvert outlet was evident where sediment bypassed the silt fence. Sediment accumulation was evident throughout the streambed and significant sediment buildup was present within the culvert outlet. I followed sediment within the streambed for approximately 50 feet below the culvert outlet (Photos 7-15).-I observed no sediment accumulation above the timber matting crossing at the culvert inlet, indicating that sediment entered the stream where it bypassed the perimeter silt fence (Photo 16).-A material stockpile staged along the access road at STA 15+00 was bordered by reinforced silt fence and was temporarily stabilized with straw (Photo 17).-A material stockpile staged along the access road at STA 18+00 was bordered by reinforced silt fence and was temporarily stabilized with straw (Photo 18).-The plugging rig was installed at the time of inspection. All equipment was staged on the plugging pad. I was unable to see if secondary containment was installed at the plugging rig due to equipment being staged close to the rig (Photos 21-22).-The plugging pad perimeter was lined with reinforced silt fence, which appeared to be functioning properly. I observed no signs of accelerated erosion around the plugging pad (Photos 23-24).Due to sediment bypassing the silt fence at STA 14+00 and entering UNT to Dunkard Creek, violations of 102.4(b)1, 102.11(a)1, 78.53, CSL 301, and CSL 307(a) are being issued.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Seneca Resources Co Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-09-16
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 862214
Permit API: 117-21688
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Delmar Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-09-16
Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection conducted a Follow-up inspection of the Seneca Resources - DCNR 007 Pad K located in Delmar Twp, Tioga Co. on 9/16/2019 @1100 hours. Activity onsite consisted of a truck removing the last temporary tank/gas buster onsite. A Nuverra vac truck was also observed parked onsite. No personnel was observed. At the time of this inspection, the pad surface appears to have been regraded. All temporary flowback equipment appears to have been removed from the site. Multiple damp areas and smalll puddles were observed on the pad surface in the vicinity of the production tanks. The field conductivity of the puddles was recorded at between 5.00mS/cm – 7.5mS/cm.(See attached photos for exact measurements and location of puddles). Courses of silt-sock were observed installed along the NE corner of the pad. Pad material appears to have been eroding off the surface down the fill slope in multiple areas. During a 5/21/19 inspection (IR#2885486) of the site, numerous puddles were discovered on the pad surface. Field screening indicated the conductivity ranged from 4 to >19.99 mS/cm. A sample was collected and upon the DEP receiving the results, they were communicated to Seneca and documented in an Administrative Inspection report (IR# 2897380) on 6/24/19. These results show elevated levels of chloride, strontium and barium indicating a release of a pollutional substance that exceeds Act 2 standards. This inspection report noted violations and requested information pertaining to the quantity of material released to the pad surface as well as what actions Seneca has done to remediate these releases. The NOV response received on 7/15/19 from Seneca failed to provide this information. Therefore, the violations cited will remain outstanding he 73H well permit. Seneca should reference 78a66(c) to determine the actions necessary to achieve compliance at this location. I departed the site @1245 hours.

PGE estimated about 2-3 barrels were spilled from the containment of the production fluid tanks secondary containment. At the time of inspection, the impacted soil had been excavated below 2,500 uS/cm. The area impacted was about 20' x 15' and about 5 inches of soil in the area has been removed. properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/23/2025
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8235155
Permit API: 015-23892
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Troy Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/27/2025
Comments: Incident Inspection of Repsol's "Broadleaf Holdings" Marcellus well site. Tory Rogers called the DEP on Friday morning May 23, 2025 to report a release of approximately 9 gallons of diesel based drilling mud released from a flare stack to the pad surface that morning. I met with Tory Rogers, Jim Brown, Megan DePue (all 3 Repsol), and Scotty Brown (DEP, OGI) on site. While drilling a future Marcellus Shale well there was a control issue, so they lit the flare stack to burn off natural gas incurred. Some drilling mud blew out of the flare stack, estimated at 7 gallons onto pad containment, and 9 gallons on the pad surface. Rogers showed us where the flare stack released drilling mud. Resource Environmental directed excavation to remove pad material the drilling mud impacted, which was approximately a 10'X60' area. They completed the cleanup around 1600 hrs the same day the release occurred. The material is in 2 dumpsters on the NE corner of the pad. I got a 1.5 ppm reading with a 10.6 eV MiniRae photoionization detector (PID) from the removed pad material, and a 0.0 ppm PID reading from the remediated pad surface, which indicates the cleanup sufficiently removed the impacted pad material. Drill cuttings in a dumpster near the drill rig gave a 135.7 ppm reading. Violations cited to the 015-23893 drilling permit are considered immediately corrected.Rogers explained they increased the density of the drill mud from 12.8 lbs/gal to 13.5 lbs/gal to provide more well control.Repsol laid the containment on this pad on February 26 thru March 3, 2025. Felt liner (130 mil thickness) went down first, then wood/steel mats. Fine gravel is used to fill gaps between the mats.Precision Drilling 110 started drilling 4 new Marcellus wells at this site on April 1 2025, and expect to finish drilling around June 10, 2025. There are also 4 existing Marcellus wells here. They drill on water based mud for the vertical section, then switch to diesel based mud for the kickoff (curve) and horizontal section.Vegetation and rock stabilize soil of the site to comply with 102.22 Permanent Stabilization. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation.Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies. Pooled water on the pad surface in 3 separate puddles has electrical conductivity (EC) of 0.68-1.7 mS/cm with an Oakton PCTS5.62FJLP

Violation ID: 8201129
Permit API: 059-25626
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Center Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/11/2024
Comments: On 9/11/2024, I conducted a follow-up inspection of the Kentor Well Pad following violations issued on 9/9/2024 for a produced fluid spill proceeding the plugging of the Kentor 8H Well (Inspection ID: 3826729, Enforcement ID). Staining as a result of produced fluid spilling onto the Kentor Well Pad was discovered on 9/6/2024 following the removal of secondary containment used in the Kentor 8H Well plugging process. Leatherwood LLC was the Operator responsible for the spill, however EQT took responsibility for spill remediation. EQT is following Act 2 cleanup protocols as it is still unknown how much produced fluid was spilled.On site at the time of inspection was SPSI and Moody and Associates. I spoke to SPSI who confirmed that the spill had originated from the secondary containment during the Kentor 8H well plugging process, however it was still unclear how much produced fluid was spilled. A hole dug near the beginning of remediation approximately 75-100 feet from the plugged well yielded in produced fluid seeping into the hole. At the time of inspection, I observed produced fluid sitting within the excavated hole. SPSI stated that they were waiting for the arrival of Moody and Associates to proceed with remediation because the origin of the remaining produced fluid was unknown.While on site I observed the following:-Leatherwood LLC and EQTs Act 9 signs were posted at the site entrance (Photos 1-2).-Discoloration in the aggregate on site was apparent where excavation and impacted material remediation occurred (Photos 3-4).-The hole excavated by SPSI early in remediation was still seeping produced fluid at the time of inspection. It was undetermined where the produced fluid was seeping from and how much remained on site that was unaccounted for. I observed high conductivity of the fluid sitting in the hole (9.20 mS/cm), and the soil below the fluid was slightly elevated but below 3 mS/cm (Photos 7-11).-Previously stained aggregate located approximately 15 feet from the excavated hole demonstrated normal conductivity, and the top layer of aggregate appeared to be scraped off (Photo 12).-The plugged Kentor 8H well was barricaded by concrete barriers and backfilled since previous inspection. I observed normal conductivity readings in areas around the concrete barriers that were previously elevated (Photos 13-18).-Rolloff boxes were staged on site with impacted material. Boxes were being hauled off site at the time of inspection (Photo 19).-A ditch installed left of the plugged well was holding rainwater at the time of inspection (Photo 20).Because an unaccounted amount of produced fluid is still seeping from the Kentor Well Pad into the excavated hole approximately 75-100 feet from the origin of the spill, violations of 91.34(A), 78a.57(a), 78a.54 and SWMA 301 remain outstanding. Additionally, The Department is requesting a copy of the Kentor 8H well plugging secondary containment plan and all maintenance and inspection records associated with the secondary containment used in the plugging process.

Comments: On August 20, 2025, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of EQT's Porter Well Pad located in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County following IR 4022927 and violations issued for a 1 barrel release of a production/reuse water.The findings are as follows:At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the Act 9 sign posted at the access road entrance with all required information posted on it. In the on-site mailbox, the Department observed an Emergency Response Plan and a Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan that had a different Operator's information posted on it. The Department recommends the Operator update the plans as applicable. The access road was observed to be stabilized with gravel and the perimeters of the well site were observed to be exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with no erosion or sedimentation issues.At the time of this inspection, the gravel in the previous area of the release appeared to have been scraped/excavated. According to the operator's NOV response, remediation (via excavation) of impacted materials was completed on July 30 2025. There appeared to be rain water puddles in the area of the previous release and scraping of the contaminated gravel. The Department did not observe a sheen in any puddles of apparent rainwater in the release area. The Department utilized a conductivity meter to screen the release area and collected the following soil conductivity readings: 0.32mS, 0.77mS, 0.48mS. These readings were found to be comparable to the background conductivity reading of 0.67 mS.Based on today's inspection, violations shall remain outstanding at thus time pending the Act 2 Final report submittal, receipt, review, and approval by the Department's Environmental Cleanup and Brownfield Program
